title: Equal-information evaluation of credit assignment in modular financial reinforcement learning
abstract: arXiv:2610.14750v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Credit assignment in modular financial reinforcement learning is difficult to evaluate because an attributed signal may improve a component loss without adding decision-relevant information or improving economic outcomes. We propose an evaluation framework combining equal-information reconstruction controls, fixed-utility comparisons and prespecified downstream guardrails. The framework is instantiated in an attribution-guided modular trading architecture and tested in three controlled studies covering update allocation, supervision-target representation and portfolio risk control. We find that residual-based allocation is exactly reproduced by an ordinary loss-budget control under the disclosed interface; direct shortfall supervision improves component prediction but fails decoded-outcome preservation; and component-wise critic supervision worsens risk-condition certainty equivalent and drawdown relative to scalar supervision under fixe

translated_title: 模块化金融强化学习中信用分配的等信息评估
translated_abstract: 模块化金融强化学习中的信用分配难以评估，因为某个归因信号可能在不增加决策相关信息或改善经济结果的情况下改善组件损失。我们提出了一个评估框架，结合了等信息重构控制、固定效用比较和预先指定的下游护栏。该框架在一个归因引导的模块化交易架构中实例化，并通过三项受控研究进行测试，涵盖更新分配、监督目标表示和投资组合风险控制。我们发现，在公开接口下，基于残差的分配可以被普通的损失预算控制完全复现；直接缺口监督改善了组件预测，但未能保持解码结果；并且在固定（条件下），组件级评论家监督相比标量监督恶化了风险条件下的确定性等价和回撤。
tldr: 该论文提出了一个结合等信息重构控制、固定效用比较和下游护栏的评估框架来评估模块化金融强化学习中的信用分配，发现基于残差的分配可被普通损失预算控制完全复现，直接缺口监督无法保持解码结果，且组件级评论家监督会恶化风险相关指标。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes an evaluation framework combining equal-information reconstruction controls, fixed-utility comparisons, and downstream guardrails for credit assignment in modular financial reinforcement learning, finding that residual-based allocation is exactly reproduced by a simple loss-budget control, direct shortfall supervision fails to preserve decoded outcomes, and component-wise critic supervision worsens risk-conditioned metrics.
